en: The Sutra Spoken by the Buddha on the Dhāraṇī for Pacifying One’s Dwelling.

Thus have I heard. At one time the Buddha was staying in the Kingdom of Śrāvastī, in the Jeta Grove, at the Anāthapiṇḍada Monastery, together with a great assembly of twelve hundred and fifty bhikṣus and a multitude of great bodhisattvas.
Together with forty thousand others were the Brahmā King, lord of the Sahā world;
Śakra Devendra; and the four Great Heavenly Kings.
The Heavenly King Dhṛtarāṣṭra, the Heavenly King Virūḍhaka,
the Heavenly King Virūpākṣa,
and the Heavenly King Vaiśravaṇa.
The Great General of the Ghost-Masters of the twenty-eight divisions,
and likewise eighty-four thousand *alida* of the various devas,
together with their sons and retinues, all came to the assembly.
At that time, passing from this Buddha-world through a hundred thousand koṭis of Buddha-lands,
there was a world named Many Flowers.
The Buddha’s name is Supreme Lamp King Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha.
He currently dwells there, preaching the Dharma.
He has dispatched two bodhisattvas: the first named Great Light and the second named Immeasurable Light.
And he addressed them, saying:
"Sons of good family, you should take this dhāraṇī mantra and go to the Sahā world to [deliver it to] Śākyamuni Buddha."
This mantra provides manifold benefits;
it can cause sentient beings to dwell in peace and security throughout the long night,
and to obtain great and wholesome advantages, physical strength, and renown.
Then he spoke the mantra, saying:
*Tadyathā | paraśure | śure | śurilleśamati mahāsamati | samante | mahāsamante | śale śarale | svāhā.* At that time, the two bodhisattvas followed the Buddha.
Having received and upheld the dhāraṇī mantra,
he vanished from the Land of Many Flowers and arrived at the Jeta Grove, in Anāthapiṇḍada’s Monastery at Śrāvastī, as swiftly as a strong man might extend or contract his arm.
Then the two bodhisattvas approached the place where the Buddha was,
prostrated themselves with their heads at his feet, withdrew to stand to one side,
and addressed the Buddha, saying:
World-Honored One, beyond a hundred thousand billion buddha-lands from this world,
there is a world named Many Flowers. There,
the Buddha is named King of the Most Victorious Lamp Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha.
He is currently preaching the Dharma and has sent us here to inquire after the World-Honored One:
whether he is free from illness and affliction, and whether his physical strength and well-being are secure.
These disciples shall not be harmed by Māras, gods, ghosts, rākṣasas, bhūtas, kumbhāṇḍas, pūtanas, or piśācas.
Whether they be hungry ghosts, asuras, garuḍas, or various types of human spirits;
whether they be gandharva ghosts,
pestilence ghosts, ghosts that cause madness, or ghosts that disturb the human mind.
Whether it be spirits that cause epidemics, or reanimated corpse-spirits,
or spirits that cause illness on the first day,
or those that cause illness on the second, third, or fourth day, up to and including those that cause illness on the seventh day.
For those who are afflicted by such calamities as spirits that constantly cause illness,
the Tathāgata Supreme Lamp King dispatches this dhāraṇī mantra.
I come to offer them to the World-Honored One,
desiring also that the sentient beings of this Sahā world may dwell in peace and security throughout the long night,
and obtain great and wholesome benefits, physical vigor, and renown.
The mantra was spoken as above.
At that time, the Buddha told Ānanda:
"You should receive, uphold, read, recite, and master it thoroughly."
One should explain, transcribe, and make offerings to this dhāraṇī mantra for the sake of others.
Why is this? It is difficult for a Buddha to appear in the world, and it is likewise extremely difficult to uphold this mantra.
Ānanda, if there are those who receive, uphold, read, recite, and master this,
they shall obtain great benefit and merit.
This is the Maṇiratna Sūtra spoken by the Buddha.
